land.text: the north-east of County Antrim, 'it took in the north-east of County Antrim'; the infobox gives 'Preceded by: Ulaid'

predecessors.note: The page gives Fergus Mór (r. 498-501) as founder and Ulaid as predecessor; the Argyll side of the kingdom has no predecessor on the page. Ulaid has no Cliopatria row (group eu-11-x).

land.text: Argyll and the western seaboard, merged with Pictland: the page says the kingdom 'merged with Pictland to form the Kingdom of Alba'

successors.note: The infobox names the Kingdom of Scotland and the Kingdom of the Isles as successors; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alba row begins in 900 with the shape (41,725 km2) it files under Dál Riata in 875-899, so 850-899 has no dossier owner (see notes).

land.text: the Inner Hebrides and the western coast taken by the Vikings: 'may record the conquest of the Inner Hebrides ... by Vikings in 847'

successors.note: The Kenneth MacAlpin page: the kingdom 'had lost its western territories in the Hebrides to the Vikings'.

capitals.name: Dunadd
capitals.note: 'The hillfort of Dunadd is believed to have been its capital' (the page names Dunollie a lesser centre); the Oengus page has the fortresses of Creic and Dunadd 'taken and burnt' in 736. Dunadd is not in the gazetteer's places table.

rulers.name: Áedán mac Gabráin
rulers.note: Succession table '574-c. 608'; the lead says c. 574 until c. 609; death 'perhaps on 17 April 609'; he 'may have been deposed, or have abdicated'.

rulers.name: Domnall Brecc
rulers.note: 'from about 629 until 642'; the table gives 629 to 13 December 642; killed at Strathcarron.

rulers.name: Domnall son of Caustantín
rulers.note: 'was king of Dál Riata from 811 to 835' (the page says this is 'argued').

rulers.name: Cináed mac Ailpín (Kenneth MacAlpin)
rulers.note: Infobox 'King of Dál Riada (841-850)' and 'King of the Picts (848-858)'; the Chronicle of Melrose has him king of the Picts in 843.

correction.text: unchanged: Cliopatria's first shape, Argyll with part of the Highland coast and the north-east of County Antrim, used for 498-539

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 498-539: Cliopatria's first Dál Riata shape begins in 540. The infobox says 'Established: 498' (Fergus Mór, r. 498-501) and the text 'founded by the legendary king Fergus Mór ... in the 5th century'; the page gives no boundary, only 'the western seaboard of Scotland and northeastern Ireland'. Cliopatria's 540 shape is used for the earlier years. The page gives no area, so no comparison with the 15,793 km2 of the shape is possible.

540-586, 15,793 km2: 20 of the 26 cells of Argyll and Bute, 14 Highland cells and 13 cells in north-east Ireland (the districts of Moyle, Ballymoney, Ballymena, Larne, Coleraine, Limavady and Magherafelt). The page: 'At its height in the 6th and 7th centuries, it covered what is now Argyll'; 'In Ireland, it took in the north-east of County Antrim'; the Cenél nGabráin 'based in Kintyre', the Cenél nÓengusa 'based on Islay', 'perhaps also Mull and Ardnamurchan'. The Áedán page: Kintyre, Cowal and Bute, northern Argyll (Cenél Loairn), Islay; 'Details of the Irish part of the kingdom are less clear'.

correction.text: Argyll and north-east Antrim without the Isle of Man, raided but not held

keyframe_review.note: 587-611, 16,559 km2 as drawn: adds the Isle of Man (2 cells) from 587. The Áedán page has him 'recorded as fighting there c. 583' after the Ulstermen left the island following Báetán's death in 581, and the Dál Riata page 'naval expeditions to Orkney and the Isle of Man'; neither says Dál Riata held the island. A raid is not drawn (Orkney, raided c. 580, is not in the shape either), so Man is removed.

correction.text: Argyll, Skye and north-east Antrim without the Isle of Man

keyframe_review.note: 612-643, 18,553 km2 as drawn: +4 cells on Skye (57.3-57.5 N) and the Isle of Man still in. The Dál Riata page: the kingdom 'later grew to include Skye' (undated; the Áedán page does not mention Skye), so 612 is Cliopatria's year (confidence 1). Man is removed as above. Mag Rath (637, with Congal Cáech of the Dál nAraidi against Domnall mac Áedo, a defeat) and two defeats by the Picts in 635 and 638 do not change the Cliopatria shape before 644.

644-749, 14,662 km2: Argyll and the Highland coast; the Antrim cells and Man are gone and one cell goes to Strathclyde, whose row begins in 644. Domnall Brecc 'lost ... lastly to Eugein I of Alt Clut at Strathcarron in 642, where he was killed'. His page does not say Irish lands were lost (page silent), and the Dál Riata page dates nothing for the Irish side beyond Mag Rath (637) and Uí Tuirtri control by the 10th century. The Dál Riata page also says the kingdom 'appears to have' become tributary to Northumbrian kings, 'not certain' to have ended at Dun Nechtain (685): a Northumbrian overlordship for Northumbria's ledger.

correction.text: Dál Riata proper: Argyll and the western seaboard, as the 644 shape, under Pictish overlordship; the rest of the Cliopatria shape is Pictland

keyframe_review.note: 750-839, 59,663 km2 as drawn (225 cells): the 644 shape (Argyll) plus all of Pictland (Highland 104 of 108 cells, Moray, Perthshire, Fife, Angus, Aberdeenshire, Stirling and Orkney 2 of 3). That is the Picts, a state Cliopatria lacks, not Dál Riata. The Oengus page: 'In the 730s, Óengus fought against Dál Riata'; Creic and Dunadd 'taken and burnt' in 736; a 741 campaign 'saw Dál Riata defeated'; 'With this Dál Riata disappears from the record for a generation'; the Dál Riata page: 'brought it under Pictish overlordship by 741'. Dál Riata proper is therefore drawn as the 644 shape under Pictish overlordship (the Picts' ledger carries the vassal tint); the page also 'argues' a king, Domnall son of Caustantín, in 811-835.

correction.text: Dál Riata proper as the 644 shape, for 840-846

keyframe_review.note: 840-874, 41,623 km2 as drawn: Pictland and Argyll without 52 cells that Cliopatria gives to its Viking settlements from 840. Valid for Dál Riata only to 846: the Dál Riata page 'may record the conquest of the Inner Hebrides ... by Vikings in 847' and the Kenneth MacAlpin page has the kingdom losing 'its western territories in the Hebrides to the Vikings'. 850-874 is not Dál Riata (the infobox 'Disestablished: 850'; 'the list of kings of Dál Riada also ends around the same time'): see the verdicts for 875 and 899.

correction.text: Argyll mainland and the eastern isles; the Inner Hebrides and the west coast are Viking

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 847-849: Dál Riata proper without the Inner Hebrides and the western coast taken by the Vikings. 'may record the conquest of the Inner Hebrides ... by Vikings in 847' (the page hedges); Cliopatria's Viking settlements shape of 840 is the cut. Cináed mac Ailpín is king of Dál Riata 841-850 and of the Picts from 843 (Kenneth page).

correction.text: the shape is real but belongs to the Picts/Kingdom of Alba precursor, not to Dál Riata, which ended in 850

keyframe_review.note: 875-898, 41,725 km2: not Dál Riata, which the infobox ends in 850. The shape is identical in size to Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alba of 900-959 (41,725 km2): it is Pictland and Argyll after the union, the kingdom the Kenneth page says 'initially held the title of King of Alba' although the title appears only 'at least 42 years after Kenneth's death' (Donald II). It needs a dossier owner for 850-899: the Kingdom of Alba dossier (starting 900 in Cliopatria) or a Picts dossier.

correction.text: belongs to the Kingdom of Alba precursor for the year 899, not to Dál Riata

keyframe_review.note: 899, 41,725 km2: as the 875 shape; the last year before Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alba row begins (900). Not Dál Riata.

region.text: the western seaboard of Scotland and north-east Ireland: Argyll and the north-east of County Antrim

ledger.note: 498: Fergus Mór founds Dál Riata. 'Established: 498' (infobox, Fergus Mór r. 498-501) and 'founded by the legendary king Fergus Mór ... in the 5th century'. The page names no boundary; Cliopatria's first shape begins in 540.

region.text: Skye: the kingdom 'later grew to include Skye'

ledger.note: 612: Dál Riata reaches Skye. The year is Cliopatria's (four cells at 57.3-57.5 N); the page says only that the kingdom 'later grew to include Skye' and the Áedán page does not mention Skye. The previous holder is not named by either page; the Picts are the reading.

region.text: one cell on the Clyde side

ledger.note: 642: Domnall Brecc is killed at Strathcarron. He 'lost ... lastly to Eugein I of Alt Clut at Strathcarron in 642, where he was killed'. Strathclyde's Cliopatria row begins in 644 with one cell of Dál Riata; the page names no land.

region.text: the north-east of County Antrim: the Irish part of the kingdom, Cliopatria cells absent from the 644 shape

ledger.note: 644: Cliopatria drops the County Antrim land. The Dál Riata page dates only the defeat at Mag Rath (637), where Domnall Brecc and Congal Cáech of the Dál nAraidi lost to Domnall mac Áedo of the Cenél Conaill, and says the Irish lands were 'under Uí Tuirtri control by the 10th century'; the Domnall Brecc page mentions no loss of Irish lands (page silent). Ulaid (or its successors) is the reading for the counterpart.

region.text: Dunadd and the Argyll heartland: 'The fortresses of Creic and Dunadd were taken and burnt'

ledger.note: 736: Óengus of the Picts takes Dunadd. The annals 'report a second campaign by Óengus against the Dál Riata' and 'The fortresses of Creic and Dunadd were taken and burnt'. The first Pictish blow was dated 731 (Óengus's son Bridei against Talorgan mac Congussa's Dál Riata) but took no recorded ground.

region.text: Dál Riata, defeated in the 'smiting' of 741

ledger.note: 741: Dál Riata is defeated and falls under Pictish overlordship. A 'smiting' campaign in 741 'saw Dál Riata defeated'; the Dál Riata page: Óengus 'brought it under Pictish overlordship by 741'. After 750 the Annals of Ulster have 'the ebbing of the sovereignty of Óengus', which the page reads as Áed Find rejecting the overlordship 'in all or part of Dál Riata' (an interpretation). The vassal tint is the Picts' to record.

region.text: the Inner Hebrides and the western coast

ledger.note: 847: the Vikings take the Inner Hebrides. The Dál Riata page: the Annals 'may record the conquest of the Inner Hebrides ... by Vikings in 847'; raids began in 795. Cliopatria cuts the same land from 840; the Kenneth page has the kingdom losing 'its western territories in the Hebrides to the Vikings'.

region.text: Argyll, merged with Pictland (without the Inner Hebrides and west coast lost to the Vikings in 847, as keyframe dal-riata_847)

ledger.note: 850: Dál Riata and Pictland become one kingdom. The Kenneth MacAlpin page: 'King of Dál Riada (841-850)', 'King of the Picts (848-858)', 'conquered the kingdom of the Picts in 843-850', 'the list of kings of Dál Riada also ends around the same time'; the Dál Riata page: the kingdom 'merged with Pictland to form the Kingdom of Alba'. The page does not say the union was complete in 843; the Pictish list ends in 849 or 850.

region.text: Dál Riata proper (without the Inner Hebrides and west coast lost to the Vikings in 847, as keyframe dal-riata_847)

ledger.note: 850: the kingdom of Dál Riata ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 850'; its land is Argyll in the new Pictish-Scottish kingdom and the Hebrides in Viking hands. Cliopatria keeps the row to 899.

wars.name: Battle of Degsastan
wars.outcome: Áedán mac Gabráin 'decisively defeated by Æthelfrith of Bernicia'; the page says the defeat 'checked its growth'.
wars.note: The Áedán page gives no year for Degsastan; the 603 comes from the Dál Riata page. Belligerent set to kingdom-of-bernicia by the reviewer of eu-11-d: the page names 'Æthelfrith of Bernicia', and Cliopatria's Northumbria row begins in 612.

wars.name: Battle of Mag Rath
wars.outcome: Domnall Brecc and Congal Cáech of the Dál nAraidi 'were defeated by Domnall mac Áedo of the Cenél Conaill'; no loss of land is recorded.
wars.note: The Dál Riata page calls it 'disastrous'. Domnall Brecc also lost to the Picts in 635 and 638.

wars.name: Battle of Strathcarron
wars.outcome: Domnall Brecc killed by Eugein I of Alt Clut at Strathcarron.

wars.name: Pictish conquest of Dál Riata
wars.outcome: Creic and Dunadd taken and burnt in 736; Dál Riata defeated in 741 and under Pictish overlordship by 741.
wars.note: Fighting recorded in 731 (Bridei), 733 (Dúngal mac Selbaig), 736 and 741; Eochaid's death in 733 leaves the overkingship unclear; 750 brought the 'ebbing' of Óengus's sovereignty.

wars.name: Viking conquest of the Inner Hebrides
wars.outcome: Sporadic raids from 795; the Pictish defeat of 839 kills Áed mac Boanta; the Annals 'may record' the conquest of the Inner Hebrides in 847.

certainty.note: No boundary of this kingdom survives in the pages opened: the Highland and Antrim limits are Cliopatria outlines; the page speaks only of 'the western seaboard of Scotland and northeastern Ireland'.

notes:
Page budget (5) spent on Dál Riata, Óengus I of the Picts, Áedán mac Gabráin, Domnall Brecc and Kenneth MacAlpin. Cliopatria's row after 750 is not Dál Riata: the 750-839 shape (59,663 km2) holds all Pictland (Highland, Moray, Perthshire, Fife, Angus, Aberdeenshire, Stirling, most of Orkney) and the 840-899 shapes (41,625 and 41,725 km2) are the Picts/Alba precursor; the 875 shape has exactly the area of Cliopatria's Kingdom of Alba of 900-959. Dál Riata proper is drawn as the 644 shape from 750 to 846. 850-899 needs an owner: the Kingdom of Alba dossier (Cliopatria 900-1293) or a new Picts dossier (slug picts, 'Picts', roughly 297-843, Kingdom of Fortriu) from the additions batch eu-11-x; this dossier uses 'picts' and 'ulaid' as counterpart slugs for states Cliopatria lacks.
Start: the infobox says 498 and the text calls Fergus Mór 'the legendary king'; the start follows the infobox with confidence 2. Ulaid is the infobox predecessor.
Pictish overlordship 741-843 (and the argued Domnall son of Caustantín, king 811-835) and Northumbrian tribute (after Mag Rath, until Dun Nechtain 685 'not certain') are vassal relations that belong to the Picts' and Northumbria's ledgers (the schema puts the vassal event in the suzerain's dossier). The Pictish conquest 736-741 is recorded here as a contest.
Antrim: the page does not say when or to whom the Irish land passed; 644 is Cliopatria's year (confidence 1). Man: raided c. 583 (Áedán page) but not held; removed from the 587 and 612 shapes. Skye: 'later' (undated); 612 is Cliopatria's year (confidence 1). The Convention of Druim Cett (575; one scholar proposes c. 590) moved no border. 839: the great Pictish defeat by Vikings killed Áed mac Boanta, a king of Dál Riata.
The Oengus page was opened under 'Oengus_I_of_the_Picts' after 'Óengus_I_of_the_Picts' failed. Places missing from the gazetteer: Dunadd (capital), and the Cliopatria-style 'Isle of Man' country form was used for Man.
